hypothesis: RH is equivalent to a density statement in a Hilbert space: with rho_theta(x) = {theta/x} - theta{1/x} for x in (0, infinity) and 0 < theta <= 1, the closed span of {rho_theta} is all of L^2(0, infinity) (Nyman 1950, Beurling 1955). Baez-Duarte reformulated it as the convergence to zero of the distance from a fixed element to the span of the first N generators, which turns RH into an approximation-theoretic rather than a statistical problem. This is the framing I would probe first, because a density statement is quantitative and can be measured, and because approximation arguments can be sensitive to a single obstruction in a way that bulk statistics cannot.
falsification_criterion: Falsified by exhibiting a finite set of coefficients for which the distance is smaller than any value the criterion rules out -- that is, the criterion is refuted by a construction, not by a measurement. For the numerical probe: the sequence of distances d_N must be non-increasing and must tend to zero if RH holds. A demonstration that d_N is bounded below by a positive constant would refute RH; a numerical trend of d_N decreasing is expected under either outcome at feasible N and is therefore NOT evidence either way. This asymmetry is the whole point and must not be blurred in reporting.
